value: Screening and stabilization required regardless of ability to pay
detail: Hospitals with emergency departments that participate in Medicare must provide an appropriate medical screening exam and stabilizing treatment for emergency medical conditions (including active labor) to anyone, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay; payment questions cannot delay screening.
source_name: CMS - Emergency Medical Treatment & Labor Act (EMTALA)

value: Patients at or below 400% FPL eligible for charity care or discount payment policies
detail: California Health and Safety Code 127405 requires each hospital to maintain charity care and discount payment policies; uninsured patients or patients with high medical costs at or below 400% of FPL are eligible to apply; hospitals may not consider the patient's monetary assets in determining eligibility.
notes: Originally enacted via the hospital fair pricing laws; SB 1276 (2013-14) among amending legislation.

detail: California Insurance Code 10123.61 (SB 910, Stats. 2018, ch. 687) prohibits issuing, amending, selling, renewing, or offering short-term limited duration health insurance in California effective January 1, 2019; federal changes to short-term plan rules do not override the state prohibition.
source_name: California Department of Insurance - Notice of Prohibition (SB 910)

value: Not insurance; membership exempts from the California mandate penalty
detail: Health care sharing ministries are not health insurance; membership for at least one day in a month qualifies as a coverage exemption (code F) from California's Individual Shared Responsibility Penalty on Form FTB 3853.
notes: Sharing ministries do not guarantee payment of medical bills.

value: 18-36 months; up to 102% of the full premium
detail: Federal law lets workers and families keep job-based group coverage temporarily after job loss, reduced hours, and other qualifying events; the enrollee usually pays the entire premium plus up to 2%.

value: Age 65+ (or qualifying disability, ESRD, or ALS)
detail: Initial Enrollment Period is the 7 months starting 3 months before the month you turn 65; some people are enrolled automatically from Social Security benefits.
notes: Medicare enrollees are not subject to the Medicaid work requirement.

detail: County welfare offices take Medi-Cal applications and make eligibility determinations; DHCS directs members to keep contact information current and respond to county letters quickly.
notes: Find your county office via the DHCS contact page.

value: County office, Covered California, or the DHCS Help Center
detail: DHCS offers a Help Center, county offices, and Covered California support for applications and questions.

item: Consequence of losing Medi-Cal for work-rule noncompliance
value: No subsidized Covered California coverage - full cost of a plan
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'Individuals who are eligible for MAGI Medi-Cal but fail to meet the work and community engagement requirements due to noncompliance will not be eligible for subsidized coverage through Covered California, even if they meet all other Medi-Cal requirements. In these circumstances, the individual will be evaluated for all other Medi-Cal programs.' The DHCS member outreach letter states the same: 'If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California.'
notes: Also stated in DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member letter. This makes satisfying the requirement the highest-value action for anyone in the MAGI New Adult Group.

item: 90-day cure period after a work-rule termination
value: Return to coverage without a new application during the 90-day cure period; reapply at any time afterward
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: existing members who cannot meet the requirement 'may return to coverage without a new application during the 90-day cure period once they provide information demonstrating compliance with the requirement. After the 90-day cure period, they can re-apply for Medi-Cal at any time.'

item: Required review of every other eligibility basis before a denial
value: County must determine whether any other basis for Medi-Cal or another insurance affordability program applies, and must offer a fair hearing
detail: WIC 14005.69(k)(1)(E) and (n), as amended by AB 2161. DHCS ACWDL 25-30 Step 4 likewise requires the county to 'first evaluate the individual's eligibility for all other Medi-Cal programs that are not subjected to work and community engagement requirements.'

item: Where to get help meeting the rule
value: County Medi-Cal office, the DHCS work-rules page, the Medi-Cal Helpline, or BenefitsCal
detail: The DHCS member outreach letter directs members to their county office (dhcs.ca.gov/COL), the work-rules page (www.dhcs.ca.gov/workrules), the Medi-Cal Helpline at (800) 541-5555, and BenefitsCal.com. It also states: 'California lawmakers have invested in new resources to help you with these new rules' and that members will receive information on paid or volunteer work, job training, and schools before the end of 2026.
notes: dhcs.ca.gov/workrules resolves to the DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page.

value: Official state benefits portal for applications, renewals, forms, document upload, and notifications
detail: The DHCS member outreach letter recommends creating a BenefitsCal account, describing it as 'the official website where you can keep track of your benefits and documents, complete forms, report changes, upload documents, read notifications, and more,' with opt-in text and email messages. The DHCS Apply page lists BenefitsCal and Covered California as the two official online application partners.

The DHCS Apply page links the county office finder for phone and in-person applications, and the DHCS eligibility chart links the same page plus Covered California support and the Medi-Cal Help Center.

value: Covered California certified enrollers, county office, and the DHCS Help Center
detail: Covered California's open-enrollment page lists free help: 'Get Help - See all the free ways to get help, from live support to in-person enrollers.' The DHCS eligibility chart links Covered California support and the Medi-Cal Help Center.
